summary: Phase 8 messaging (verified-only buyer↔seller DMs, listing-tied threads, polling, unread badge, in-chat report, notifications) tested end-to-end across backend (pytest, 15/15 pass) and frontend (Playwright, two sessions owner + buyer2 + one fresh unverified). All requested testids present and wired: message-btn, chat-shell, chat-listing-link, chat-conduct, message-input, message-send-btn, report-open-btn, report-modal, report-reason-select, report-note-input, report-submit-btn, thread-back-btn, messages-page, thread-row-{id}, thread-unread-{id}, nav-messages, nav-unread-badge. Public-handle layer verified — buyer sees 'First Unit Owner' + Verified badge, no email/real-name leak. Verified-only gate confirmed on both API (403 for unverified /threads, /threads/{id}, /messages, /messages/unread-count, /notifications) and UI (fresh unverified register lands on /verification and cannot reach /messages; nav-messages link hidden). Owner correctly sees NO message-btn on own listing. Reporting: invalid reason returns 400; all 5 valid codes (scam_fraud, prohibited_item, harassment, spam, other) return 200 and create a report record. Non-participant guard: admin (verified 3rd party) gets 404 on both GET /threads/{id} and POST /threads/{id}/messages. Unread flow: buyer sends → owner sees nav-unread-badge=1 + thread-unread badge in inbox; opening thread clears both (GET marks read). Reply from owner → visible to buyer. Notifications endpoint returns 'message' type entry with correct thread_id. SMS is mocked as expected — no error path in message send.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py /api/messages/unread-count: builds `thread_id: {"$in": [...]}` via an inline `async for` list comprehension which loads every thread id twice per poll (poll every 10s per client). Prefer a single aggregate ($lookup) or cache the participant thread-id list. Cheap now, will matter at scale.

server.py post_message returns immediately after _deliver_message; email + SMS are awaited inline inside _deliver_message, so a slow Resend/Twilio provider will block the sender's HTTP response. Consider fire-and-forget via asyncio.create_task or a background queue so message send latency isn't provider-bound.

server.py active-viewing check uses `last_viewed[recipient_id]` on the thread doc snapshot passed into _deliver_message — but that snapshot was read BEFORE the send. For start_thread the thread is re-fetched, but for post_message the caller passes the pre-fetch snapshot, so last_viewed there is fresh (OK). Just worth a comment.
Thread.jsx polls every 4s regardless of tab visibility — add `document.visibilityState==='visible'` gate to avoid needless traffic on background tabs (same issue as AppNav 10s poll).
Thread.jsx report modal: no keyboard Esc handler and the report-note-input has no maxLength UI hint though backend caps at 2000.

Messages.jsx / Thread.jsx: no error toast when the /threads or /threads/{id} poll fails — silently sets empty/notFound. If the connection drops mid-session, the UI degrades to 'Conversation not found' with no retry.
AppNav.jsx unread poll: only 10s cadence, so after sending a reply the sender's own OTHER threads' unread indicators can lag up to 10s; acceptable but worth documenting.
